reviewer.model_configuration_as_exposed: Parent-inherited model and reasoning configuration; no override selected. Actual model/version and decoding settings not exposed.
reviewer.proposer_identity_as_supplied: Different fresh semantic author /root/c5b_semantic_resolution; proposed label pairs and reasoning deliberately withheld for this blind judgment.

review_method.contract: If the context is semantically ambiguous, determine whether a narrowly justified revision of the calibration context can remove ambiguity without changing the intended testing objective.
review_method.intended_testing_objective: An author/title association must be selected from the user note, with that unresolved selection being a mandatory query condition rather than irrelevant background narration. The originally authored decision stratum is AMBIGUOUS. The reviewer must independently decide whether a proposed revision legitimately serves that objective.
review_method.executable_derivation: true exactly for EXECUTABLE or EXECUTABLE_WITH_NOTICE; false for all other permitted typed_decision values

actual_task_file_reads.operation: ReadAllBytes for input/query hashes and structured output assembly

audit.tool_usage: Two exec_command calls: the first read only the allowed packet; the second reread only that packet, computed local hashes and wrote this review. No parser/evaluator/model/policy invocation or test was performed.

aggregate.explanation: All five originals are independently executable under their explicit supported filters. Each candidate narrowly repairs the authored mandatory-mapping objective and independently requires AMBIGUOUS with executable=false. The two literal-author replacements are accepted for their specific objective-linked necessity, not under a general permission to alter constraints. Corpus admission remains subject to the untouched downstream gates.

cases.disposition_scope: Semantic revision and independently derived labels only; downstream corpus admission gates are not established by this review.

original.normative_explanation: The title and remaining supported filters are explicit. The two-author note describes uncertain background but never makes selection of its associated author a query requirement. The supplied rules therefore permit execution without resolving that anecdote.

candidate.normative_explanation: The by-clause makes the author paired with the requested title a mandatory filter. Either supplied name could be associated with that title; the note gives no unique pairing and there is no external bibliographic evidence. An explicit title does not discharge the separately required selection from the note. Clarification is required. This is ambiguity of an existing required reference, rather than an absent task component, unsupported capability or contradiction.

author_resolution.reference: author my note pairs with the requested title
author_resolution.absence_mask_semantics: False means an author requirement is present; null resolved_author denotes unresolved identity, not permission to omit the filter.

candidate.clarification_target: Which named author does the note pair with the requested title?

revision.necessity_and_proportionality: Adding exactly one relational authorship condition is necessary to turn the previously optional note uncertainty into the mandatory author-selection problem specified by the testing objective. It preserves the note, requested title, every existing filter and operating context. This is a proportionate repair of the defective calibration context, not a claim that the original user already requested this condition.

eligibility.explanation: The revised case directly exercises a mandatory unresolved author-title mapping with otherwise supported constraints. Shared wording across cases is visible, but corpus-level duplicate/isolation status cannot be inferred from this restricted packet. Acceptance does not waive those gates.

revision.necessity_and_proportionality: Replacing the explicit by Yvren Mosveil clause with the note-dependent author condition changes a literal operand, so it cannot be accepted as meaning-preserving paraphrase. It is nevertheless justified under the supplied revision contract: the old clause supplies the very author value whose unresolved selection the calibration objective is intended to test. The replacement is confined to that conflicting author-selection mechanism, retains both names and the uncertain note, and preserves the title, every non-author filter and operating context. Keeping the old literal would preserve an already selected author and fail to cleanly instantiate this intended selection problem. The candidate remains in the intended AMBIGUOUS stratum; no author is invented or inferred.
